sentences.text: In the previous chapter, you built and pretrained a GPT-style model and used it for next-token generation; here the focus shifts from training a model from scratch to loading released GPT-2 weights into that same architecture and then adapting it for a supervised classification task.

That shift matters because you load the publicly released OpenAI GPT-2 weights into the GPT model built earlier, and pretraining is not the end of working with a language model because those pretrained weights can be fine-tuned for specific applications such as email classification.

We begin with why these pretrained weights are useful, what assumptions they bring with them, and which extra tools are needed to work with OpenAI's TensorFlow-formatted release from a PyTorch-based codebase.

From there, the chapter walks through the released GPT-2 files, the settings and tokenization metadata, the structure of the parameter dictionary, and how those weights map onto the model class you already have.

The second half turns to classification: preparing the spam dataset, handling tokenization and padding, building dataloaders, attaching a classification head, checking accuracy and loss before training, running the fine-tuning loop, reviewing the results and overfitting checks, and finally using and saving the fine-tuned model.
The same GPT architecture and model class built earlier can be reused with publicly released GPT-2 weights.

OpenAI saved the GPT-2 weights in TensorFlow, while the surrounding code uses PyTorch, so this setup installs TensorFlow and "tqdm", with TensorFlow version at least 2.15 and "tqdm" version at least 4.66.

The main loading function in "gpt_download3.py" downloads seven GPT-2 files, locates the latest checkpoint, loads the checkpoint parameters into a dictionary named "params", and returns that along with a "settings" dictionary.

Among the released files, "encoder.json" maps tokens to token IDs, the GPT-2 vocabulary has 50,257 tokens, and "hparams.json" stores settings such as vocabulary size, context length, embedding dimension, attention heads, and transformer blocks.

For the fine-tuning project, the model takes email text as input and predicts whether the message is spam or not spam, and fine-tuning means starting from pretrained GPT-2 weights and training the model again on task-specific data.
